whyWrongByChoice.B: Five percent underestimates the mortality the brick cites once overt shock has developed.
whyWrongByChoice.D: Fifty percent overstates the mortality; the brick cites a figure approaching 20%.
whyWrongByChoice.E: Eighty percent greatly overstates the mortality of anaphylactic shock.

questions.stem: A 45-year-old man develops sneezing, nasal congestion, and itchy eyes whenever he visits his daughter, who recently adopted a cat. Skin prick testing is positive for cat dander. He has never had eczema or asthma, and no one in his family has allergic disease. His physician tells him his allergy is not atopic. Which of the following best explains this statement?

choices.label: A
choices.text: Allergic symptoms can occur without a genetic predisposition to IgE sensitization

choices.label: B
choices.text: Atopy applies only to allergies that first begin during early childhood

choices.label: C
choices.text: Atopy requires a documented history of anaphylaxis to a specific allergen

choices.label: D
choices.text: His reaction is mediated by IgG rather than IgE, so it is not a true allergy

choices.label: E
choices.text: Reactions to animal dander are never IgE-mediated and are therefore irritant

explanation.summary: Not all individuals with allergic disease have atopy; symptoms can occur without the genetic predisposition.
explanation.whyCorrect: The brick states that not all individuals with allergic diseases have underlying atopy, meaning symptoms can still occur but they are not genetically linked. Atopy usually implies a personal or family history of atopic dermatitis, allergic rhinitis, and asthma, which this patient lacks.

whyWrongByChoice.B: The brick defines atopy by genetic predisposition and personal or family history, not by age of onset.
whyWrongByChoice.C: Atopy is a genetic predisposition to IgE sensitization, not a history of anaphylaxis.
whyWrongByChoice.D: His positive skin prick test indicates an IgE-mediated type 1 reaction; the absence of atopy does not change the mechanism.
whyWrongByChoice.E: Animal dander is listed among the most common inhaled allergens driving IgE-mediated reactions.

questions.stem: A 9-month-old infant develops hives and vomiting within 20 minutes of being fed a new food for the first time. Which of the following is the most common cause of orally ingested food allergy?

explanation.summary: Milk is the number one cause of orally ingested food allergy, followed by egg whites.
explanation.whyCorrect: The brick lists common orally ingested allergens with milk as the #1 cause and egg whites as the #2 cause, followed by cereal grains (wheat), legumes (peanuts, soybeans), tree nuts (hazelnuts), and seafood.

whyWrongByChoice.A: Egg whites are the second most common cause of food allergy, behind milk.
whyWrongByChoice.C: Peanuts are legumes and a common allergen but rank below milk and egg whites.
whyWrongByChoice.D: Seafood is a common ingested allergen but is not the most common cause.
whyWrongByChoice.E: Cereal grains such as wheat are common food allergens but are not the leading cause.

questions.stem: A 4-year-old boy is newly sensitized to peanut after repeated exposure. Dendritic cells in his gut mucosa take up peanut protein, process it into peptides, and present them to a T-cell subset that secretes IL-4, IL-5, and IL-13 and drives B cells to class-switch to IgE. Which of the following is this T-cell subset?

explanation.summary: Th2 cells, secreting IL-4, IL-5, and IL-13, drive B cells to class-switch to IgE during allergic sensitization.
explanation.whyCorrect: The brick describes allergen encountered by a transmucosal route being taken up by an antigen-presenting cell such as a dendritic cell, processed into peptides, and presented to Th2 cells. Th2 cells, capable of secreting IL-4, IL-5, and IL-13, interact with B cells and drive them to class-switch to IgE.

whyWrongByChoice.A: Cytotoxic T cells kill infected or abnormal cells; they do not drive B-cell class switching to IgE.
whyWrongByChoice.B: Natural killer cells are not T cells and do not interact with B cells to drive IgE class switching.
whyWrongByChoice.C: Regulatory T cells suppress immune responses rather than driving IgE production.
whyWrongByChoice.D: Th1 cells are not the subset the brick assigns to driving IgE class-switching in allergy.

questions.stem: An allergist counsels several patients that the first step in managing their allergies is to avoid their identified allergens whenever practical. Allergy to which of the following is most easily managed by avoidance?

explanation.summary: Orally ingested allergens are the most easily avoided, whereas avoidance is virtually impossible for most inhaled allergens.
explanation.whyCorrect: The brick states that orally ingested allergens are most easily avoided (although hidden ingredients in foods can trigger reactions), while avoidance is virtually impossible for most inhaled allergens because, for example, pollen and fungal spores are essentially ubiquitous. Egg whites are an ingested allergen; the other choices are inhaled allergens.

whyWrongByChoice.A: Animal dander is an inhaled allergen, and the brick states avoidance is virtually impossible for most inhaled allergens.
whyWrongByChoice.B: Dust mites are among the most common inhaled allergens, for which avoidance is virtually impossible.
whyWrongByChoice.D: Fungal spores are inhaled allergens described as essentially ubiquitous and virtually impossible to avoid.
whyWrongByChoice.E: Pollen is an inhaled allergen the brick describes as essentially ubiquitous, making avoidance virtually impossible.

questions.stem: A 25-year-old woman with allergic asthma develops wheezing within minutes of entering a house with a cat. Her wheezing resolves after an albuterol inhaler, but 6 hours later, after she has left the house, she develops recurrent wheezing and chest tightness. Which of the following best explains the delayed recurrence of her symptoms?

choices.label: A
choices.text: A second release of pre-formed histamine from mast-cell granules

choices.label: C
choices.text: Delayed class-switching of B cells to IgE

choices.label: D
choices.text: Persistence of tryptase in the serum for several hours

choices.label: E
choices.text: Release of newly synthesized cytokines and lipid mediators

explanation.summary: The late-phase response is delayed because its mediators (cytokines, chemokines, and lipid mediators) must be newly synthesized.
explanation.whyCorrect: The brick describes two phases of mast cell degranulation. In the late phase response, newly synthesized molecules are released, and the synthesis itself causes the delay. These include cytokines and chemokines (TNF-alpha, IL-4, IL-13, IL-5, GM-CSF) and lipid mediators (leukotrienes C4, D4, E4 and PAF).

whyWrongByChoice.A: Histamine is a pre-formed mediator of the early phase, released immediately on cross-linking; the late phase is not a second histamine release.
whyWrongByChoice.B: Heparin is a pre-formed early-phase toxic metabolite; the brick does not attribute delayed bronchoconstriction to it.
whyWrongByChoice.C: Class-switching to IgE occurs during sensitization, before any reaction, not hours after exposure.
whyWrongByChoice.D: Tryptase persisting in serum is a diagnostic marker of mast cell activation, not the cause of delayed symptoms.

questions.stem: A 32-year-old man with peanut anaphylaxis receives intramuscular epinephrine with rapid improvement in his wheezing and blood pressure. The emergency physician then administers methylprednisone. Which of the following best explains the rationale for adding the corticosteroid?

choices.label: A
choices.text: Blockade of H1 histamine receptors to relieve pruritus and urticaria

choices.label: B
choices.text: Immediate reversal of histamine-induced hypotension and shock

choices.label: C
choices.text: Neutralization of free IgE before it binds to FcepsilonRI on mast cells

choices.label: D
choices.text: Rapid bronchodilation of the constricted airways within minutes

choices.label: E
choices.text: Suppression of cytokine and lipid mediator synthesis in the late phase

explanation.summary: Corticosteroids are given because of the late-phase reaction; they suppress synthesis of cytokines and inhibit production of lipid mediators.
explanation.whyCorrect: The brick states the late-phase reaction is the reason for the use of anti-inflammatory corticosteroids, which suppress synthesis of cytokines like interleukins and inhibit production of lipid mediators. In anaphylaxis, the steroid is part of the cocktail that also helps reduce late-phase reactions.

whyWrongByChoice.A: H1 receptor blockade is the mechanism of antihistamines such as diphenhydramine.
whyWrongByChoice.B: Reversal of hypotension is achieved by epinephrine through alpha-receptor vasoconstriction, not by steroids.
whyWrongByChoice.C: Binding free IgE to prevent attachment to FcepsilonRI is the mechanism of omalizumab.
whyWrongByChoice.D: Rapid bronchodilation is the action of beta-agonists such as epinephrine and albuterol; steroids act by modulating gene transcription.

questions.stem: A 38-year-old landscaper had a systemic reaction after a wasp sting and is referred to an allergist to confirm venom allergy before starting immunotherapy. Which of the following testing methods is most commonly used for venom allergy?

choices.label: A
choices.text: Epicutaneous skin prick testing with venom extract

choices.label: C
choices.text: Intradermal injection of diluted allergen extract

choices.label: D
choices.text: Serum enzyme immunoassay for venom-specific IgE

explanation.summary: Intradermal skin testing, injecting a small amount of diluted allergen extract, is the technique most used for drug and venom testing.
explanation.whyCorrect: The brick distinguishes skin prick/puncture tests from intradermal injection by method and by the allergens they typically identify. Intradermal skin testing injects a small amount of diluted allergen extract with a needle and syringe and is most used for drug and venom testing. Positive results in all types are a wheal-and-flare reaction.

whyWrongByChoice.A: Skin prick testing is the most common and sensitive method overall, but the brick identifies intradermal testing as the technique most used for venom.
whyWrongByChoice.B: Flow cytometry identifies specific cell lineages, not which allergens cause a reaction.
whyWrongByChoice.D: Enzyme immunoassays can measure allergen-specific IgE but are less sensitive than skin testing and are not the technique most used for venom.
whyWrongByChoice.E: Challenge testing is risky, especially with a history of anaphylaxis, and is not the standard approach to venom allergy testing.

questions.stem: A 19-year-old woman undergoes skin prick testing on her back for suspected pollen allergy. Fifteen minutes later, the site pricked with birch pollen extract shows a raised, pale, itchy bump surrounded by a zone of redness. Which of the following best describes this finding?

explanation.summary: A positive skin test of any type is a wheal-and-flare reaction.
explanation.whyCorrect: The brick states that positive results in all types of skin testing (prick/puncture and intradermal) are a wheal-and-flare reaction, indicating IgE-mediated sensitization to the tested allergen.

whyWrongByChoice.A: Angioedema is the deeper swelling seen in anaphylaxis (lips, tongue, throat), not the localized positive skin test response.
whyWrongByChoice.B: An eczematous rash is a skin manifestation of allergic disease such as atopic dermatitis, not the acute test-site reaction.
whyWrongByChoice.C: Flushing is diffuse skin redness seen in anaphylaxis, not a localized raised bump with surrounding erythema.
whyWrongByChoice.D: Induration is a firm thickening and is not how the brick describes a positive allergen skin test.

questions.stem: A 30-year-old woman has year-round nasal congestion and sneezing that is worst on waking, and her history strongly suggests dust mite allergy. A serum enzyme immunoassay for dust-mite-specific IgE is negative. Which of the following is the most appropriate next step to identify her trigger?

choices.label: B
choices.text: Conclude that dust mites are not her trigger

choices.label: D
choices.text: Repeat the enzyme immunoassay in 6 months

explanation.summary: Currently available enzyme immunoassays are less sensitive than skin testing, so a negative blood test does not exclude allergy when suspicion is high.
explanation.whyCorrect: The brick states that ELISA/EIA can measure allergen-specific IgE in serum, but the currently available EIAs are less sensitive than skin testing. Skin prick testing is the most common and most sensitive method to identify specific allergens, so it is the appropriate next step.

whyWrongByChoice.A: Immunotherapy should not begin without first identifying the specific allergen with definitive testing.
whyWrongByChoice.B: Because EIA is less sensitive than skin testing, a negative result does not rule out dust mite allergy; history alone is also insufficient for diagnosis.
whyWrongByChoice.C: Challenge testing is riskier and is not the primary choice for identifying specific allergens.
whyWrongByChoice.D: Repeating a less sensitive test after a delay does not address the sensitivity limitation.

questions.stem: A 35-year-old woman is treated in the emergency department for anaphylaxis after a hornet sting. She receives intramuscular epinephrine, a steroid, and diphenhydramine, and her symptoms resolve. Which of the following is the most appropriate plan at discharge?

choices.label: A
choices.text: Begin subcutaneous venom immunotherapy in the emergency department

choices.label: B
choices.text: Perform intradermal venom testing in the emergency department

choices.label: C
choices.text: Prescribe daily oral prednisone for the next year

choices.label: D
choices.text: Prescribe self-injectable epinephrine and refer for allergen skin testing

choices.label: E
choices.text: Recommend a supervised venom challenge within the next week

explanation.summary: After anaphylaxis, patients are discharged with a self-injectable epinephrine device and referred to an allergist for skin testing.
explanation.whyCorrect: In the brick's case, MJ is given a prescription for an EpiPen and instructed how to use it before leaving the emergency department, and is instructed to see an allergist for skin testing. The brick notes prognosis has improved with public awareness of devices for self-administration of epinephrine.

whyWrongByChoice.A: Immunotherapy for proven IgE-dependent venom anaphylaxis is started by an allergist after testing, not in the emergency department.
whyWrongByChoice.B: Allergen identification is done by an allergist in follow-up, not in the emergency department during the acute visit.
whyWrongByChoice.C: Steroids are part of the acute treatment cocktail to reduce late-phase reactions; a year of daily prednisone is not the discharge plan.
whyWrongByChoice.E: Challenge testing is risky, especially in a patient with a history of anaphylaxis, and is not the recommended follow-up.

questions.stem: A 40-year-old man with allergic rhinitis has profuse rhinorrhea that persists despite an antihistamine. His physician adds an intranasal medication that reduces nasal secretions by preventing acetylcholine-induced effects on airway tissue. Which of the following is the mechanism of the added medication?

choices.label: D
choices.text: Blockade of the CysLT1 leukotriene receptor

explanation.summary: Muscarinic antagonists such as ipratropium and tiotropium block M3 receptors, preventing acetylcholine-induced bronchoconstriction and reducing nasal secretions.
explanation.whyCorrect: The brick states muscarinic antagonists block M3 receptors on airway smooth muscle, preventing acetylcholine-induced bronchoconstriction, which can be beneficial in allergic asthma or rhinorrhea. These agents help reduce nasal secretions and improve airflow; examples include ipratropium and tiotropium.

whyWrongByChoice.A: Binding free IgE is the mechanism of omalizumab.
whyWrongByChoice.B: Glucocorticoid receptor binding is the mechanism of steroids such as fluticasone, which act through gene transcription rather than blocking acetylcholine.
whyWrongByChoice.D: CysLT1 blockade is the mechanism of montelukast and zafirlukast, which act on leukotriene effects rather than acetylcholine.
whyWrongByChoice.E: Beta-2 stimulation is the mechanism of beta-agonists such as albuterol, which cause bronchodilation, not reduced nasal secretions.

questions.stem: A 12-year-old girl with allergic asthma and allergic rhinitis is prescribed montelukast. Which of the following mediators has its effects blocked by this drug?

explanation.summary: Montelukast and zafirlukast are leukotriene receptor antagonists that block the CysLT1 receptor, preventing bronchoconstriction, mucus secretion, and eosinophil recruitment.
explanation.whyCorrect: The brick states leukotriene receptor antagonists block the cysteinyl leukotriene receptor (CysLT1), preventing the effects of leukotrienes such as bronchoconstriction, mucus secretion, and eosinophil recruitment. They are particularly useful in allergic asthma and allergic rhinitis; montelukast and zafirlukast are the commonly used agents.

whyWrongByChoice.A: Acetylcholine effects at M3 receptors are blocked by muscarinic antagonists such as ipratropium.
whyWrongByChoice.C: Histamine effects are blocked at H1 receptors by antihistamines, not by montelukast.
whyWrongByChoice.D: Platelet-activating factor is a late-phase lipid mediator, but montelukast blocks the leukotriene receptor, not PAF.
whyWrongByChoice.E: Tryptase is a mast cell enzyme used as a diagnostic marker; montelukast does not target it.

questions.stem: A pharmacology student is classifying allergy medications by the location of their molecular target. Which of the following medications acts by binding an intracellular receptor rather than a cell-surface receptor?

explanation.summary: Steroids such as fluticasone bind intracellular glucocorticoid receptors and modulate gene transcription.
explanation.whyCorrect: The brick states steroids bind to intracellular glucocorticoid receptors and modulate gene transcription to suppress production of pro-inflammatory cytokines and mediators, reducing swelling, mucus production, and immune cell recruitment. Commonly used steroids include fluticasone, prednisone, and methylprednisone.

whyWrongByChoice.A: Albuterol is a selective beta-2 agonist acting on adrenergic receptors of bronchial smooth muscle.
whyWrongByChoice.B: Cetirizine is an antihistamine that blocks histamine H1 receptors on the cell surface.
whyWrongByChoice.D: Tiotropium is a muscarinic antagonist that blocks M3 receptors on airway smooth muscle.
whyWrongByChoice.E: Zafirlukast is a leukotriene receptor antagonist that blocks the CysLT1 receptor.

questions.stem: A 36-year-old woman has had daily hives for 9 months with no identifiable trigger. Her symptoms have not responded to standard therapy with antihistamines. Which of the following is the most appropriate targeted therapy?

explanation.summary: Omalizumab is used for chronic spontaneous urticaria unresponsive to standard therapy, in addition to moderate-to-severe allergic asthma.
explanation.whyCorrect: The brick states omalizumab, a monoclonal antibody that binds free IgE, is used in moderate-to-severe allergic asthma and in chronic spontaneous urticaria unresponsive to standard therapy, reducing the frequency and severity of allergic symptoms.

whyWrongByChoice.A: Albuterol treats bronchospasm; it has no role in urticaria.
whyWrongByChoice.B: Montelukast is described as particularly useful in allergic asthma and allergic rhinitis, not chronic urticaria.
whyWrongByChoice.D: Immunotherapy requires an identified allergen and is used for allergic rhinitis, asthma, venom, and medication allergy, not spontaneous urticaria without a trigger.
whyWrongByChoice.E: Tiotropium is a muscarinic antagonist used for airway smooth muscle and nasal secretions, not skin disease.

questions.stem: A 27-year-old man with allergic rhinitis due to dust mites, tree pollen, cat dander, and mold is recommended immunotherapy. He asks for sublingual tablets so he can avoid injections. Which of the following is the most accurate counseling?

choices.label: A
choices.text: Immunotherapy is ineffective for inhaled allergens

choices.label: B
choices.text: Subcutaneous immunotherapy is available for a wider variety of allergens

choices.label: C
choices.text: Sublingual immunotherapy is the most commonly used form

choices.label: D
choices.text: Sublingual immunotherapy shifts the response toward IgE rather than IgG

choices.label: E
choices.text: Sublingual products are available for essentially all allergens

explanation.summary: Subcutaneous immunotherapy is the most commonly used route and covers a variety of allergens, whereas oral and sublingual forms are limited to a handful of FDA-approved allergens.
explanation.whyCorrect: The brick states subcutaneous injection is the most commonly used form of immunotherapy and is available for a variety of allergens, while oral and sublingual forms, although often preferred by patients for their noninvasiveness, are limited to a handful of FDA-approved allergens.

whyWrongByChoice.A: Immunotherapy is effective in managing allergic rhinitis and asthma with a T1HSR component, which involve inhaled allergens.
whyWrongByChoice.C: Subcutaneous, not sublingual, is the most commonly used form of immunotherapy.
whyWrongByChoice.D: Desensitization by any route shifts the response away from IgE toward milder IgG or IgA responses.
whyWrongByChoice.E: Oral and sublingual immunotherapy is limited to a handful of FDA-approved allergens, not essentially all.

questions.stem: A 50-year-old woman with a documented IgE-mediated allergy to an antibiotic requires that same antibiotic because it is the only effective treatment for her infection. Her allergist plans immunotherapy (desensitization) to the medication. By which of the following routes is immunotherapy for IgE-mediated medication allergy administered?

explanation.summary: Immunotherapy is the preferred treatment for IgE-mediated medication allergy, and for medications it is given orally or intravenously rather than injected.
explanation.whyCorrect: The brick states immunotherapy is the preferred treatment for proven IgE-dependent insect venom anaphylaxis and IgE-mediated medication allergy, and that variations exist for different allergies; for example, immunotherapy for IgE-mediated medication allergies is oral or IV, not injected.

whyWrongByChoice.A: Inhalation is a challenge testing method, not the route of medication desensitization.
whyWrongByChoice.B: Intradermal injection is a skin testing technique for drug and venom allergy, not an immunotherapy route.
whyWrongByChoice.D: Subcutaneous injection is the most common route for immunotherapy in general, but the brick specifies medication allergy immunotherapy is not injected.
whyWrongByChoice.E: Sublingual immunotherapy is limited to a handful of FDA-approved allergens and is not the route described for medication allergy.

questions.stem: A 29-year-old man with allergic rhinitis and asthma with a type 1 hypersensitivity component begins subcutaneous immunotherapy to grass pollen. He asks whether he can now stop his inhaled corticosteroid and antihistamine. Which of the following is the most appropriate response?

choices.label: A
choices.text: He may stop all medications as soon as immunotherapy begins

choices.label: B
choices.text: Immunotherapy eliminates the need for allergen avoidance

choices.label: C
choices.text: Immunotherapy is not effective for asthma

choices.label: D
choices.text: Immunotherapy supplements medications rather than replacing them

choices.label: E
choices.text: The benefits of immunotherapy end as soon as injections stop

explanation.summary: Immunotherapy is not recommended as the sole treatment for allergic rhinitis and asthma; it is used as a supplement to medications.
explanation.whyCorrect: The brick states immunotherapy is effective in managing allergic rhinitis and asthma with a component of T1HSR, but it is not recommended as the sole treatment for these conditions and is used as a supplement to medications.

whyWrongByChoice.A: Because immunotherapy is a supplement to medications rather than a replacement, stopping all medications is inappropriate.
whyWrongByChoice.B: Avoidance remains the first step in managing allergies whenever practical; immunotherapy does not eliminate it.
whyWrongByChoice.C: Immunotherapy is effective in managing asthma with a component of T1HSR.
whyWrongByChoice.E: The brick states the benefits of immunotherapy may last for years after treatment is stopped.

questions.stem: A 22-year-old woman eats a cookie containing hidden tree nuts and within 10 minutes develops diffuse hives, swelling of the lips and throat, abdominal cramping, nausea, and vomiting. Which of the following mechanisms of anaphylaxis is most directly responsible for this group of symptoms?

explanation.summary: In anaphylaxis, vascular leakage is responsible for hives, throat swelling, abdominal discomfort, nausea, vomiting, and diarrhea.
explanation.whyCorrect: The brick attributes the manifestations of anaphylaxis to three effects of released histamine and cytokines: bronchoconstriction (wheezing, dyspnea, coughing, respiratory distress), vasodilation (tachycardia, hypotension, lightheadedness), and vascular leakage (hives, throat swelling, abdominal discomfort, nausea, vomiting, diarrhea). This patient's symptoms fit vascular leakage.

whyWrongByChoice.A: Alpha-1 activation is the therapeutic action of epinephrine that reduces edema and vascular permeability; it does not cause these symptoms.
whyWrongByChoice.B: Bronchoconstriction causes wheezing, dyspnea, coughing, and respiratory distress rather than hives and gastrointestinal symptoms.
whyWrongByChoice.C: Eosinophil recruitment by IL-5 contributes to late-phase tissue damage, not the immediate hives and swelling of anaphylaxis.
whyWrongByChoice.E: Vasodilation is responsible for tachycardia, hypotension, and lightheadedness, none of which are described here.

questions.stem: A 48-year-old man is brought to the emergency department with sudden onset of diffuse hives, throat swelling, wheezing, and a blood pressure of 82/50 mm Hg. He denies any known allergies and cannot identify any recent exposure to a new food, medication, or insect sting. Which of the following is the most appropriate approach?

choices.label: A
choices.text: Await a serum tryptase result before starting treatment

choices.label: B
choices.text: Diagnose anaphylaxis clinically and treat immediately

choices.label: C
choices.text: Exclude anaphylaxis because no allergen exposure is identified

choices.label: D
choices.text: Order a serum enzyme immunoassay for specific IgE before treating

choices.label: E
choices.text: Perform skin prick testing to identify the trigger first

explanation.summary: Anaphylaxis is diagnosed on clinical signs and symptoms and should be suspected even without a history of allergen exposure.
explanation.whyCorrect: The brick states anaphylaxis is diagnosed based on clinical signs and symptoms: suspect it when a patient has cardiovascular, respiratory, or GI symptoms, or skin features of hives and angioedema, within minutes to hours after allergen exposure. It also states anaphylaxis should be suspected in a patient who presents with any of these symptoms without a history of allergen exposure. Diagnosis must be prompt.

whyWrongByChoice.A: Tryptase is useful when the diagnosis is uncertain, but treatment with epinephrine should not be delayed for a laboratory result.
whyWrongByChoice.C: The brick explicitly states anaphylaxis should be suspected even without a history of allergen exposure.
whyWrongByChoice.D: Serum IgE immunoassays identify allergens for later management and do not guide emergency treatment.
whyWrongByChoice.E: Skin testing identifies specific allergens in follow-up with an allergist; it has no role during an acute life-threatening reaction.

questions.stem: A 45-year-old man is evaluated after an episode of flushing and hypotension. Serum tryptase drawn during the episode was elevated. Three weeks later, while he is completely asymptomatic, a repeat serum tryptase remains markedly elevated. Which of the following is the most likely explanation for the persistently elevated tryptase?

explanation.summary: Elevated tryptase is not specific to anaphylaxis; it also occurs in systemic mastocytosis and other mast-cell activation syndromes.
explanation.whyCorrect: The brick states tryptase, produced primarily by mast cells, can be elevated within minutes and persist for several hours after allergy or anaphylaxis begins, but elevated tryptase can also occur in other conditions such as systemic mastocytosis and other mast-cell activation syndromes. A tryptase that remains markedly elevated weeks later in an asymptomatic patient points to one of these conditions rather than a transient anaphylactic episode.

whyWrongByChoice.A: An anaphylactoid reaction is an acute, non-IgE anaphylaxis-type event; it would not explain a persistently elevated tryptase while asymptomatic weeks later.
whyWrongByChoice.B: Atopy is a genetic predisposition to IgE sensitization and does not itself produce a persistently elevated tryptase.
whyWrongByChoice.C: Tryptase elevation from anaphylaxis persists for several hours, not weeks, and the patient is asymptomatic.
whyWrongByChoice.D: Allergic rhinitis is a localized allergic disease and is not described as a cause of persistently elevated serum tryptase.

questions.stem: A 26-year-old man with anaphylaxis after a bee sting receives intramuscular epinephrine, diphenhydramine, and a steroid in the emergency department. Thirty minutes later his hives, wheezing, and hypotension have fully resolved, and he asks to go home. Which of the following is the most appropriate next step?

choices.label: A
choices.text: Discharge now with an oral antihistamine

choices.label: B
choices.text: Observe for several hours for delayed responses

choices.label: C
choices.text: Perform a venom challenge to confirm the trigger

choices.label: D
choices.text: Perform skin prick testing before discharge

explanation.summary: After anaphylaxis symptoms resolve, patients should be monitored for several hours for medication efficacy and any delayed responses.
explanation.whyCorrect: The brick states patients should be monitored for several hours after initial symptoms resolve for medication efficacy and any delayed responses, and that management includes observation for several hours with possible additional administration of epinephrine.

whyWrongByChoice.A: Immediate discharge misses the observation period the brick recommends for delayed responses.
whyWrongByChoice.C: Challenge testing is risky, especially with a history of anaphylaxis, and is not used to confirm the trigger after an acute episode.
whyWrongByChoice.D: Skin testing is arranged with an allergist in follow-up, not performed before discharge from the emergency department.
whyWrongByChoice.E: Venom immunotherapy is started by an allergist after IgE-dependent venom anaphylaxis is proven, not during the acute visit.
